title: Watch it work
intro: WioGenie is easier to understand by running it than by reading about it. This is an illustrative walkthrough of how it investigates a production incident — the sequence and the citation behaviour are real; the incident itself is a composite, not a customer one.
incident: 02:14 — repayment notification failures spike to 4% on the SME lending topic. On-call is paged.

steps.action: Reads the alert and decides which sources are worth opening.
steps.finding: Consumer-side failure, not a delivery-provider outage. Fans out to code, logs and history.

steps.action: Scans the consumer group around the spike.
steps.finding: Rebalance storm — the group rebalanced 14 times in nine minutes. Failures cluster inside those windows.

steps.action: Opens the consumer and reads the commit history around it.
steps.finding: max.poll.interval.ms is unchanged, but a template lookup added last week made processing slower per message.

steps.action: Searches Jira and past RCAs for the same signature.
steps.finding: Seen once before, eleven months ago, on a different service. Same cause: work per message outgrew the poll interval.
steps.citation: TES-19442 · RCA: consumer rebalance under slow handlers

steps.action: Assembles the answer and checks every claim carries a source.
steps.finding: Slower per-message work pushed processing past max.poll.interval.ms; the broker assumed the consumer was dead and rebalanced. Retries then landed mid-rebalance and failed.

conclusion: Root cause in under a minute, with every claim traceable to a log line, a file or a prior RCA. The citation trail is the product: it is what lets a responder disagree with the machine quickly, instead of trusting it slowly.
